iss.name: International Space Station
iss.imageCredit: Image: NASA via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
iss.blurb: The International Space Station is the biggest thing humans have ever built in space — as long as a football field! Astronauts from many countries live and work there, doing science experiments that float.
iss.funFact: The ISS zooms around Earth so fast it sees 16 sunrises and sunsets every single day!

tiangong.name: Tiangong Space Station
tiangong.imageCredit: Image: Shujianyang via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
tiangong.blurb: Tiangong means “Heavenly Palace” in Chinese. It’s China’s space station, where taikonauts live and run science experiments high above Earth.
tiangong.funFact: Tiangong is shaped like a giant letter “T” — three big modules locked together in orbit!

hubble.name: Hubble Space Telescope
hubble.imageCredit: Image: NASA via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
hubble.blurb: Hubble is a school-bus-sized telescope floating in space. Because it looks at the stars from above Earth’s blurry air, its pictures are super sharp — it has taken over 1.5 million of them!
hubble.funFact: Astronauts visited Hubble five times to give it new cameras and parts — like doctor checkups for a telescope!

starlink.name: Starlink Satellite
starlink.imageCredit: Image: Wikideas1 via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
starlink.blurb: Starlink satellites work as a giant team to beam internet down to Earth. They help ships at sea, airplanes, and remote villages get online.
starlink.funFact: There are thousands of Starlink satellites — the biggest satellite family ever launched!

oneweb.name: OneWeb Satellite
oneweb.imageCredit: Image: Kim Shiflett via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
oneweb.blurb: OneWeb satellites beam internet to the far corners of the planet, including the Arctic. They fly near the poles so they can see the whole Earth.
oneweb.funFact: OneWeb satellites were built on a super-fast assembly line — up to two satellites per day!

kuiper.name: Project Kuiper Satellite
kuiper.imageCredit: Image: U.S. Space Force photo by Gwendolyn Kurzen via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
kuiper.blurb: Project Kuiper is Amazon’s plan to bring fast internet to places that don’t have it. Its satellites will form a giant network circling Earth.
kuiper.funFact: Kuiper is named after the Kuiper Belt — a ring of icy objects far beyond Neptune!

iridium.name: Iridium Satellite
iridium.imageCredit: Image: Flickr user ideonexus via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
iridium.blurb: Iridium satellites carry phone calls and text messages from the most remote places on Earth — even the middle of the ocean!
iridium.builder: Iridium Communications (built by Thales Alenia Space)
iridium.funFact: Early Iridium satellites sometimes flashed super bright in the night sky. Skywatchers called them “Iridium flares”!

goes.name: GOES Weather Satellite
goes.imageCredit: Image: Ben Smegelsky via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
goes.blurb: GOES weather satellites stare at Earth without blinking from 22,000 miles up. They track hurricanes, wildfires, and lightning so forecasters can warn people in time.
goes.funFact: A GOES satellite can photograph the entire United States in just 30 seconds!

terra.name: Terra (Earth Observer)
terra.imageCredit: Image: NASA via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
terra.blurb: Terra is NASA’s Earth-watching superstar. It maps pollution, melting ice, and growing crops — basically giving our planet a daily checkup.
terra.funFact: “Terra” means “Earth” in Latin — and it has watched over Earth for more than 25 years!

aqua.name: Aqua (Earth Observer)
aqua.imageCredit: Image: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
aqua.blurb: Aqua studies Earth’s water — oceans, clouds, ice, and rain. It helps scientists understand how water moves around our planet.
aqua.funFact: “Aqua” means “water” in Latin, and Aqua flies in formation with other satellites like a team!

noaa20.name: NOAA-20 (JPSS)
noaa20.imageCredit: Image: NOAASatellites via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
noaa20.blurb: NOAA-20 is a weather and climate watchdog. It takes super-detailed pictures of clouds, ice, and ocean temperatures to make forecasts better.
noaa20.funFact: NOAA-20 flies from pole to pole, seeing the whole Earth twice every day!

suominpp.name: Suomi NPP
suominpp.imageCredit: Image: Ryan Zuber, Scientific Visualization Studio via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
suominpp.blurb: Suomi NPP watches Earth day and night, tracking wildfires, air pollution, and sea ice. It can even see city lights glowing from space!
suominpp.funFact: It’s named after Verner Suomi, known as the father of satellite weather-watching!

metop.name: MetOp Weather Satellite
metop.imageCredit: Image: European Space Agency via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0 igo)
metop.blurb: MetOp is Europe’s polar weather satellite. It helps make the multi-day forecasts you see on TV more accurate.
metop.funFact: MetOp data is shared freely with weather services all over the world!

dmsp.name: DMSP Weather Satellite
dmsp.blurb: DMSP satellites have watched Earth’s weather since the 1960s — one of the longest-running satellite programs ever.
dmsp.builder: U.S. Space Force (built by Lockheed Martin)
dmsp.funFact: DMSP satellites can see the aurora — the northern lights — glowing from space!

sentinel3.name: Sentinel-3
sentinel3.imageCredit: Image: SkywalkerPL via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
sentinel3.blurb: Sentinel-3 is Europe’s ocean and land monitor. It measures sea level, ocean color, and land temperature for scientists.
sentinel3.funFact: Sentinel-3 can spot a wildfire from space and measure how hot it is burning!

meteorm.name: Meteor-M Weather Satellite
meteorm.imageCredit:
Image: El Salvador.

The original uploader was El Salvador at Russian Wikipedia. via Wikimedia Commons (CC0)
meteorm.blurb: Meteor-M is Russia’s weather satellite. It photographs clouds and ice to help forecasters across Russia and beyond.
meteorm.funFact: Some Meteor satellites also listen for distress signals from ships and hikers in trouble!

elektrol.name: Elektro-L
elektrol.imageCredit: Image: MKonair via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
elektrol.blurb: Elektro-L is Russia’s round-the-clock weather watcher. It sits in one fixed spot over the equator, snapping a full-Earth photo every 30 minutes.
elektrol.funFact: Elektro-L’s camera takes pictures in colors our eyes can’t even see!

fengyun.name: Fengyun Weather Satellite
fengyun.imageCredit: Image: Jakub Hałun via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
fengyun.blurb: Fengyun means “wind and cloud” in Chinese. These satellites help China track typhoons, floods, and droughts.
fengyun.funFact: Fengyun satellites have been flying since 1988 — one of the world’s oldest weather satellite families!

insat3d.name: INSAT-3D
insat3d.imageCredit: Image: Indian Space Research Organisation via Wikimedia Commons (GODL-India)
insat3d.blurb: INSAT-3D is India’s weather eye in the sky. It watches monsoon clouds and helps warn people about cyclones.
insat3d.funFact: INSAT-3D can photograph all of India in just a few minutes!

kosmos.name: Kosmos Satellite
kosmos.imageCredit: Image: Linar Khalitov via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
kosmos.blurb: “Kosmos” is the name given to hundreds of Soviet and Russian satellites — spies, science labs, and test craft flying secret missions.
kosmos.funFact: More than 2,500 satellites have been named Kosmos — more than any other name in space history!

jwst.name: James Webb Space Telescope
jwst.imageCredit: Image: NASA via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
jwst.blurb: The James Webb Space Telescope is the biggest, most powerful telescope ever launched. It sees the universe’s first galaxies with heat vision!
jwst.builder: NASA · ESA · CSA (built by Northrop Grumman)
jwst.funFact: Webb’s sunshield is as big as a tennis court and keeps its mirrors colder than Pluto!

chandra.name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
chandra.imageCredit: Image: NASA/CXC/NGST via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
chandra.blurb: Chandra is NASA’s X-ray telescope. It sees the hottest, most violent places in the universe — exploding stars and giant black holes!
chandra.funFact: Chandra is named after Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, who figured out how stars die!

landsat9.name: Landsat 9
landsat9.imageCredit: Image: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center/Conceptual Image Lab via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
landsat9.blurb: Landsat 9 photographs every inch of Earth’s land every 16 days. Farmers, firefighters, and scientists all use its pictures.
landsat9.funFact: The Landsat program has photographed Earth non-stop for over 50 years — the longest space photo album ever!

gps3.name: GPS III Satellite
gps3.imageCredit: Image: U.S. Air Force via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
gps3.blurb: GPS III satellites are the newest helpers for your phone’s maps. They broadcast super-precise timing signals from 12,000 miles up.
gps3.builder: U.S. Space Force (built by Lockheed Martin)
gps3.funFact: Your phone figures out where you are by timing signals from at least four GPS satellites at once!

intelsat.name: Intelsat Communications Satellite
intelsat.imageCredit: Image: NASA via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
intelsat.blurb: Intelsat runs one of the world’s biggest TV and internet satellite fleets. Its satellites beam shows and data across oceans.
intelsat.funFact: Intelsat helped broadcast the first Moon landing to the whole world in 1969!

voyager1.name: Voyager 1
voyager1.imageCredit: Image: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
voyager1.blurb: Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object ever — over 15 billion miles away! It carries a golden record with Earth sounds, music, and greetings.
voyager1.funFact: Voyager 1’s radio signal takes over 22 hours to reach Earth — even traveling at the speed of light!

falcon9.name: Falcon 9
falcon9.imageCredit: Image: U.S. Space Force photo by Joshua Conti via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
falcon9.blurb: Falcon 9 is SpaceX’s workhorse rocket. Its first stage lands itself back on Earth and flies again — like a boomerang!
falcon9.funFact: A single Falcon 9 booster has flown more than 20 missions!

falconheavy.name: Falcon Heavy
falconheavy.imageCredit: Image: Daniel Oberhaus via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
falconheavy.blurb: Falcon Heavy is three Falcon 9 boosters strapped together. It can lift huge satellites — and once launched a car toward Mars!
falconheavy.funFact: Its first flight carried a Tesla Roadster with a dummy driver named Starman!

starship.name: Starship
starship.imageCredit: Image: Steve Jurvetson via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
starship.blurb: Starship is the biggest, most powerful rocket ever built — taller than the Statue of Liberty! SpaceX designed it to carry people to the Moon and Mars.
starship.funFact: Starship’s booster is caught mid-air by giant mechanical arms nicknamed “chopsticks”!

newglenn.name: New Glenn
newglenn.imageCredit: Image: U.S. Space Force photo by Senior Airman Samuel Becker via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
newglenn.blurb: New Glenn is Blue Origin’s giant reusable rocket, named after John Glenn — the first American to orbit Earth.
newglenn.funFact: New Glenn is so big its nose cone could fit a whole school bus inside!

vulcan.name: Vulcan Centaur
vulcan.imageCredit: Image: NASA/Ben Smegelsky via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
vulcan.blurb: Vulcan Centaur is the United Launch Alliance’s newest rocket. It replaced the famous Atlas and Delta rockets.
vulcan.funFact: Vulcan’s first flight carried a robotic lander heading for the surface of the Moon!

electron.name: Electron
electron.imageCredit: Image: NASA Kennedy Space Center / Rocket Lab via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
electron.blurb: Electron is Rocket Lab’s small, speedy rocket for tiny satellites. It’s one of the first rockets with a 3D-printed engine!
electron.funFact: Electron is only about as tall as a five-story building — a mini rocket with a big job!

soyuz.name: Soyuz
soyuz.imageCredit: Image: NASA Headquarters / NASA/Bill Ingalls via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
soyuz.blurb: Soyuz is the world’s most-flown rocket family, launching since the 1960s. It has carried more people to space than any other rocket.
soyuz.funFact: Soyuz is based on the R-7 — the rocket that launched Sputnik, the very first satellite ever!

ariane6.name: Ariane 6
ariane6.imageCredit: Image: GOES imagery: CSU/CIRA & NOAA via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
ariane6.blurb: Ariane 6 is Europe’s newest big rocket, launching science missions and satellites from the jungles of South America.
ariane6.funFact: Ariane rockets launched famous space telescopes — including the James Webb Space Telescope!

longmarch5.name: Long March 5
longmarch5.imageCredit: Image: China News Service via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
longmarch5.blurb: Long March 5 is China’s most powerful rocket. It launched the pieces of China’s space station and a rover to Mars!
longmarch5.funFact: It’s nicknamed the “chubby one” because it’s wider than other Chinese rockets!

sls.name: Space Launch System
sls.imageCredit: Image: https://www.nasa.gov/marshall/ via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
sls.blurb: NASA’s Space Launch System is the rocket for the Artemis Moon missions. It’s the most powerful rocket NASA has ever built.
sls.funFact: SLS’s first flight sent a capsule around the Moon and back — with no crew aboard!

pad39a.name: Kennedy Space Center LC-39A
pad39a.imageCredit: Image: NASA/Jamie Peer via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
pad39a.blurb: Launch Complex 39A is the most famous launch pad on Earth! Apollo 11 left for the Moon from here, and so did the first Space Shuttle.
pad39a.funFact: SpaceX now launches astronauts to the space station from this historic pad!

padslc40.name: Cape Canaveral SLC-40
padslc40.imageCredit: Image: U.S. Space Force SLD45 by Gwendolyn Kurzen via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
padslc40.blurb: Space Launch Complex 40 is SpaceX’s busiest pad — rockets lift off here almost every week!
padslc40.funFact: A Dragon capsule once carried a wheel of cheese to orbit as a joke — it launched from nearby pads like this one!

padslc4e.name: Vandenberg SLC-4E
padslc4e.blurb: Space Launch Complex 4 East sits on the California coast. Rockets here fly south over the ocean to reach polar orbits.
padslc4e.funFact: From Vandenberg you can watch rockets climb right over the Pacific Ocean!

padstarbase.name: Starbase, Texas
padstarbase.imageCredit: Image: Jenny Hautmann via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
padstarbase.blurb: Starbase is SpaceX’s Texas home for Starship — the biggest rocket ever. Future Mars missions will start here!
padstarbase.funFact: Starbase has a giant tower with “chopsticks” arms that catch the rocket booster mid-air!

padmahia.name: Mahia — Rocket Lab LC-1
padmahia.imageCredit: Image: Rodney Allen via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
padmahia.blurb: Launch Complex 1 sits on New Zealand’s Mahia Peninsula — the first privately-owned orbital launch site in the world.
padmahia.funFact: It’s one of the only orbital launch pads in the Southern Hemisphere!

padkourou.name: Guiana Space Centre
padkourou.imageCredit: Image: Denys via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)
padkourou.blurb: The Guiana Space Centre is Europe’s spaceport in South America. Being near the equator, Earth’s spin gives rockets an extra push!
padkourou.funFact: The James Webb Space Telescope launched from Kourou on Christmas Day 2021!

padtanegashima.name: Tanegashima Space Center
padtanegashima.imageCredit: Image: ウニウニ via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
padtanegashima.blurb: Tanegashima is Japan’s beautiful island spaceport. Rockets launch over the ocean, past palm trees and beaches.
padtanegashima.funFact: Tanegashima has launched missions to the Moon and to asteroids!

padjiuquan.name: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center
padjiuquan.imageCredit: Image: 中国新闻社 via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
padjiuquan.blurb: Jiuquan is China’s first spaceport, out in the Gobi Desert. China’s astronauts — taikonauts — ride rockets to space from here.
padjiuquan.funFact: China’s first satellite launched from Jiuquan in 1970!

padbaikonur.name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
padbaikonur.imageCredit: Image: Bill Ingalls via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
padbaikonur.blurb: Baikonur is the world’s oldest spaceport — Sputnik and Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space, launched from here!
padbaikonur.funFact: Baikonur sits in Kazakhstan, and Russia leases it — real space history lives here!
